title: Khalsa Sovereignty and the Kasur Episode Opening

blocks.text: This transition page first closes the Lakhmi Narayan episode by stressing how deeply Khalsa collection had cut into Sirhind revenue. In the exchange with Abdali and Ala Singh, the Khalsa insists that sovereignty had already been granted to the Khalsa by their Guru, so it is not a favor to be requested from any emperor.

That closing argument turns the page from revenue and diplomacy toward a fresh martial narrative. The poem explicitly asks the reader to listen to the episode about the city of Kasur, where a new grievance will test whether the Panth will act on its claims of protection and rule.

By the end of the page, the Dal Khalsa forces set up camp near the Amritsar shrine and the focus settles on Hari Singh Bhangi and the congregational life around Amritsar. The page is therefore a hinge between one political episode and the opening scene of the first Kasur invasion.
